title: Lesson 80 - Could We Bring This Back to the Main Point?

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: We have thirty minutes and one decision: whether the revised framework is safe and useful enough to authorize planning. We are not assigning shifts or accepting bookings today.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Let me summarize where we are. The one-year goal is an evidence-based operating decision, not automatic expansion. The revised proposal fits the eight-hundred-dollar and twenty-hour ceilings.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: Before we decide, I want the staffing assumption stated accurately. I said protected coverage was possible under some rotas; I did not say every Tuesday was easy to cover.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: That’s not how your comment appeared in my first summary. I wrote “Tuesday coverage is available.” Thank you for correcting it.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Can we compare the wording before we continue?

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: My note says, “Tuesday is workable if no closer is scheduled to open the next morning and two people volunteer for that date.” The condition matters.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: I’ll correct the record to “potentially workable subject to date-specific coverage.” No shift will be treated as available until the people involved confirm it.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Good. Can we hear from Malik on the revised menu and group size before Rosa responds to the cost question?

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: Twelve guests and three preordered items protect preparation time. My remaining concern is that a late cancellation could use staff hours without producing a full trial.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: The deposit reduces that risk, and a cancellation still produces limited evidence about the booking process. I would not count it as a completed service trial.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: We’re moving into ideas about new signs again. Could we bring this back to the main point? Do the current controls make four smaller trials more useful than two larger ones?

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: Four dates give us more process observations, but only if staffing is voluntary and each cancellation is labelled separately. Two larger trials would tell us more about capacity above twelve.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: The evidence most relevant to this decision is whether the core process can operate inside the fixed limits. It does not need to answer the larger-group question yet.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: A possible objection is that the smaller design may make the proposal look easier than a real recurring model would be.

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: That’s a fair point. I would qualify the conclusion by saying the pilot can test a bounded occasional-booking model only; it cannot justify a recurring or larger service.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: With that limitation in the record, I support the four-trial option. What I need you to understand is that schedule consent must be a gate, not an action item someone can fill in later.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Agreed. Before we move on, are we ready to decide on the framework with that gate, a review after trial two and an automatic pause if cost, hours or recovery protection would be exceeded?

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.text: Yes. I’ll own the planning sheet and evidence log. Owen remains the decision owner, and Malik will check that the written schedule condition matches what staff actually confirm.

lines.speaker: Malik
lines.text: I agree, provided my review does not make me responsible for finding cover. Each person still accepts or declines a proposed shift directly.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Then the framework is approved under those conditions. Is this an accurate record of the decision: up to four smaller trials over six weeks, no more than twelve guests, a limited preordered menu, eight hundred dollars, twenty extra hours, voluntary date-specific staffing, review after trial two and pause before any limit is crossed?

transfer.title: Noor's booking inquiry
transfer.instruction: Listen twice without reading. Record the group size, requested dates, services, decision status and unknowns before giving a neutral 60-second summary.
transfer.speaker: Noor
